question.problem:
The joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ for the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given in the table below. Find $\text{E}[2XY].$

| $f$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=4$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $0.1$ | $0.25$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.25$ | $0.4$ |
question.worked_solution:
Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are discrete random variables with supports ${S}_{X}$ and ${S}_{Y},$ respectively, and $f(x,y)$ is their joint probability mass function with support $S={S}_{X}\times {S}_{Y}.$ If $r:{R}^{2}\to R$ is a function of two variables, then the rule of the lazy statistician states that

$$
\text{E}[r(X,Y)]={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}r(x,y)\,f(x,y).
$$

In our case, we have

$$
r(x,y)=2xy.
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[2XY] & ={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}r(x,y)\,f(x,y) \\  & =(2\cdot 1\cdot 2)\cdot f(1,2)+(2\cdot 1\cdot 4)\cdot f(1,4)\,+(2\cdot 2\cdot 2)\cdot f(2,2)+(2\cdot 2\cdot 4)\cdot f(2,4) \\  & =4\cdot f(1,2)+8\cdot f(1,4)+8\cdot f(2,2)+16\cdot f(2,4) \\  & =4\cdot 0.1+8\cdot 0.25+8\cdot 0.25+16\cdot 0.4 \\  & =0.4+2+2+6.4 \\  & =10.8.\end{aligned}
$$
